newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nearly 11,000 Albanians flee to Italy, Greece -- UN.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 11,000 Albanians flee to Italy, Greece -- UN.

text.p: More than 1,000 Albanians are fleeing armed chaos in their troubled Balkan country every day for Italy and Greece, bring the total to nearly 11,000 so far, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday.
Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole said more than 7,000 Albanians had fled to Italy and some 3,500 to Greece. "There's a steady exodus of 1,000 people a day," she told a briefing.

The UNHCR, which is urging both governments to give the refugees temporary asylum and register them, is especially worried about unaccompanied children, including a four-month-old baby found on board a ship bound for Italy. Military deserters and those without papers are also of concern.
The UNHCR was also concerned about criminals arriving in Italy, which has a big problem with clandestine immigration from Albania, often involving drug-smuggling.
The arrivals in Italy included 1,300 Albanians who sailed to Bari in the south overnight in a flotilla of ramshackle boats.

Port authorities said 629 Albanians reached Bari early on Tuesday aboard three fishing boats. Down the coast, 487 arrived on a single boat which limped into harbour with engine problems. A further 214 people came in on two trawlers.
O'Toole said 120 boats with Albanians had arrived so far in Italy, where authorities had also registered 342 military men.
The UNHCR had no reports of refugees fleeing to other countries.
Italy was hit by an exodus of tens of thousands of Albanians in 1991 after communist rule crumbled. It has said it will grant refugees only temporary sanctuary.

Maki Shinohara, a UNHCR spokeswoman, said her agency was worried about the fate of refugees sailing to Italy in rough seas. U.S. Navy forces in the Adriatic picked up 85 Albanians from two stricken boats on Sunday, including one which capsized with 55 men on board who had to be rescued by Marine and Navy swimmers.
